verdict.line: You lose trades and the solo-kill race to K'Sante's shorter cooldowns and R (All Out) all-ins before level 6, but Malphite's 56.7% head-to-head win rate over 60 games shows the lane swings your way once Sunfire Aegis and Thornmail come online.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes) on an 3.5s cooldown and E (Footwork) on a 10-8s cooldown let him initiate far more trades per minute than you can answer, and his R (All Out) knockback-through-wall engage makes early solo kills his to take. Malphite's Passive (Granite Shield) recharge and E (Ground Slam)'s armor-scaled damage let you absorb that aggression rather than win it outright. The 56.7% head-to-head win rate over 60 games says you are not fighting for lane dominance, you are fighting to survive it and let your build take over.

theirWindow.what: At 2 stacks of Ntofo Strikes his Q fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in, chaining into W (Path Maker)'s stun. Back out of range before the second stack lands instead of trying to walk it off.

yourWindow.when: when his E and W are both down
yourWindow.what: With Footwork (10-8s cd) and Path Maker (14-10s cd) on cooldown, K'Sante has no dash, shield, or stun to answer you. Step up and land Q (Seismic Shard) and E (Ground Slam) for free poke.

Full build and ultimate decide teamfights, not duels

start.why: K'Sante's early pressure is auto- and poke-based; the regen and damage reduction against low-damage hits blunt his Q line strikes and let Granite Shield recharge between pokes.

boots.why: K'Sante's damage is physical and auto-reliant for stacking Dauntless Instinct marks; flat reduction on his attacks matters more here than magic resist.

core.why: Gives you waveclear and sustained damage to punish his cooldown-down windows while adding health and armor against his auto-based trading.
Directly counters an AD, on-hit-marking opponent and turns his aggressive trading pattern against him.
The cooldown reduction and armor let you close the gap on his faster ability rotation and shut down his auto damage output.

situational.when: he rushes lifesteal or you're bleeding health to on-hit marks before your first core item completes
their team adds magic damage poke on top of K'Sante's physical pressure
the game goes long and you need more flexible resistance scaling over a fourth armor item
you're ahead and want to amplify Ground Slam and ultimate burst for a more proactive engage pattern

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustains you through the repeated auto trades K'Sante forces early, stacking health permanently so his poke matters less over time. Master-tier Malphite players instead run Arcane Comet across 1,232 games, which suits a more poke-first style landing Q (Seismic Shard) from range rather than absorbing extended trades; stick with Grasp if you expect to be in his face all lane.

summoners.why: Teleport is run in 82.9% of games here because this is a lane you survive rather than win outright; it lets you reset after bad trades and still arrive for scaling items and side-lane pressure. Flash+Ignite (60% win rate, 13.2% pick) is the alternative if you plan to punish his 3.5s Q cooldown windows aggressively enough to force an early kill.

playing.title: Hold until 2 Q stacks
playing.detail: Watch K'Sante's Ntofo Strikes stack counter and disengage before the second stack, since it fires a pulling shockwave that chains into his stun.

playing.title: Trade only when E and W are down
playing.detail: Step in with Q (Seismic Shard) and E (Ground Slam) only once Footwork and Path Maker are both on cooldown, since he has no dash or stun to punish you in that window.

playing.title: Let him commit first before 6
playing.detail: Granite Shield recharges when you haven't been hit recently; bait his auto-stacking instead of initiating, since solo-kill advantage is his through level 5.

playing.title: Respect All Out at level 6
playing.detail: His R knocks you through walls and transforms his kit into a faster, harder-hitting dash combo. Stay near turret range or hold Flash until your own cooldowns are up.

playing.title: Rush Sunfire for tempo
playing.detail: Sunfire Aegis first lets you push waves and out-sustain his poke, forcing him to either match your pressure or lose tempo.

playing.title: Save R for his all-in, not yours
playing.detail: Use Unstoppable Force reactively to catch him mid-All Out rather than opening with it, since his R grants him speed that lets him close distance faster than you during that window.

playing.title: Play for the midgame, not first blood
playing.detail: Don't force all-ins levels 1-5; last-hit clean and let Thornmail and Frozen Heart turn the 56.7% head-to-head number into a real lead.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the cooldown-window and trade-pattern reasoning is my own analysis, not measured data.
